import pytest
from your_module import group_by  # Replace with the actual module name


class TestGroupByHappyPath:
    """Tests for typical, expected use cases of group_by."""

    def test_group_by_attribute(self):
        """Group items by a specific attribute."""
        data = [
            {"name": "Alice", "age": 30},
            {"name": "Bob", "age": 25},
            {"name": "Charlie", "age": 30},
        ]
        result = group_by(data, key_fn=lambda x: x["age"])
        expected = {
            30: [{"name": "Alice", "age": 30}, {"name": "Charlie", "age": 30}],
            25: [{"name": "Bob", "age": 25}],
        }
        assert result == expected

    def test_group_by_identity(self):
        """Group items using the item itself as the key."""
        data = ["apple", "banana", "apple", "cherry", "banana"]
        result = group_by(data, key_fn=lambda x: x)
        expected = {
            "apple": ["apple", "apple"],
            "banana": ["banana", "banana"],
            "cherry": ["cherry"],
        }
        assert result == expected

    def test_group_numbers_by_parity(self):
        """Group numbers by a computed property (even/odd)."""
        data = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
        result = group_by(data, key_fn=lambda x: "even" if x % 2 == 0 else "odd")
        expected = {
            "odd": [1, 3, 5],
            "even": [2, 4, 6],
        }
        assert result == expected

    def test_group_by_length(self):
        """Group strings by their length."""
        data = ["cat", "dog", "elephant", "ant", "bee"]
        result = group_by(data, key_fn=len)
        expected = {
            3: ["cat", "dog", "ant", "bee"],
            8: ["elephant"],
        }
        assert result == expected

    def test_preserves_insertion_order_of_keys(self):
        """
        Keys should appear in the order they are first encountered.
        (This relies on Python 3.7+ dict insertion order preservation.)
        """
        data = [3, 1, 2, 1, 3]
        result = group_by(data, key_fn=lambda x: x)
        keys = list(result.keys())
        assert keys == [3, 1, 2]


class TestEdgeCases:
    """Tests for edge case inputs to group_by."""

    def test_empty_list(self):
        """An empty list should produce an empty dictionary."""
        result = group_by([], key_fn=lambda x: x)
        assert result == {}

    def test_single_element(self):
        """A single-element list groups correctly."""
        data = [42]
        result = group_by(data, key_fn=lambda x: x)
        assert result == {42: [42]}

    def test_all_same_key(self):
        """When all items produce the same key, they group into a single list."""
        data = [10, 20, 30]
        result = group_by(data, key_fn=lambda x: "same")
        assert result == {"same": [10, 20, 30]}

    def test_all_unique_keys(self):
        """When every item has a unique key, each value list has length 1."""
        data = [1, 2, 3]
        result = group_by(data, key_fn=lambda x: x * 10)
        assert result == {10: [1], 20: [2], 30: [3]}

    def test_does_not_mutate_original_list(self):
        """The original list should remain unchanged after grouping."""
        data = [1, 2, 3]
        original = data.copy()
        group_by(data, key_fn=lambda x: x)
        assert data == original

    def test_key_fn_returning_tuple(self):
        """Keys can be tuples, which are hashable."""
        data = [[1, 2], [3, 4], [1, 2]]
        result = group_by(data, key_fn=tuple)
        expected = {
            (1, 2): [[1, 2], [1, 2]],
            (3, 4): [[3, 4]],
        }
        assert result == expected

    def test_key_fn_with_external_state(self):
        """Test key_fn that uses external counter (closure)."""
        counter = 0

        def key_fn(x):
            nonlocal counter
            counter += 1
            return x

        data = ["a", "b", "a"]
        result = group_by(data, key_fn=key_fn)
        assert counter == 3
        assert result == {"a": ["a", "a"], "b": ["b"]}
